reply.answer_text: For business protection with three shareholders, each owner takes out an own-life Lifelong Protection policy written in a business trust for the co-owners. The cross-option agreement gives the estate a put option (the right to sell the shares) and the surviving shareholders a call option (the right to buy). This structure preserves Business Relief on the shares. When one shareholder dies, the trustees receive the policy proceeds and the survivors can buy the shares under the option.
